title: Permanent live IDs & version control
subtitle: One live identity. Numbered archives. Restore in place.
headline: ONE LIVE FILE ID. EVERY GOVERNED REVISION REMEMBERED.
motto: ARCHIVE THE VERSION. KEEP THE LIVE ID.
core_rule: For each subject governed by the JP numbered-archive policy, find and reuse its original populated live file. Never create a replacement live source during routine revisions. Before a meaningful change save an enumerated PRE copy, edit the SAME live file ID, validate and provider-read back the original, then save an enumerated POST copy. Archive copies have their own IDs and versioned filenames; the original live ID stays stable.
filename_rule: Rename only archive copies to carry ordinal and PRE/POST. Do not rename the original or manufacture a new live ID as a version number.
sequence_rule: Each owning source maintains its own monotonically enumerated snapshot ordinal. Sheet versions, Google Docs revisions, Colab notebook snapshots, Git commits/tags, A7 sequences, and software releases are independent namespaces. Never infer synchronized version numbers.

workflow.label: RESOLVE LIVE
workflow.detail: Identify the owning project, subject, provider, exact original file ID, authority and access permissions.

workflow.label: READ BACK
workflow.detail: Fetch the populated current original; record provider ID, revision, filename, original link and source hash where possible.

workflow.label: NUMBER + PRE
workflow.detail: Choose the next ordinal in that subject's dedicated archive. Create a PRE copy with a versioned filename BEFORE changing the original.

workflow.label: EDIT ORIGINAL
workflow.detail: Apply authorized edits to the SAME live provider object ID or governed Git source path; never switch all links to a duplicate.

workflow.label: VALIDATE + READBACK
workflow.detail: Run relevant owner-specific checks and read back the same provider ID/revision. Report failures without claiming approval.

workflow.label: NUMBER + POST
workflow.detail: After checks, create the matching ordinal POST copy. Verify POST content corresponds to the validated live state.

workflow.label: MANIFEST + RESTORE
workflow.detail: Append what/why/source IDs/revisions/links/evidence/checks/uncertainties to version-history. Restore older content INTO original live ID when authorized.

source_types.name: Google Docs
source_types.archive: Separate named Google Doc copies: 000001_PRE, 000001_POST, etc.
source_types.qualification: Google's native revision history also exists; archive copies do not supersede the original.

source_types.name: Google Colab notebook
source_types.live: Original notebook Drive file ID, .ipynb or notebook URL
source_types.archive: Numbered .ipynb/notebook copies in that subject's central archive
source_types.qualification: Keep runnable code/cells in original notebook; distinguish notebook-copy ordinal from a Git code release.

source_types.name: Google Sheets
source_types.live: Original spreadsheet file ID, tabs/ranges and native revision
source_types.archive: Numbered whole-workbook PRE/POST copies when required by owner policy
source_types.qualification: Humans continue editing original Sheets. Never replace live cells with CSV or website output.

source_types.name: Excel / PDF / CAD / other Drive files
source_types.live: Original provider file ID plus appropriate revision/hash
source_types.archive: Enumerated complete copies in dedicated archive with extension retained
source_types.qualification: File conversion may lose semantics; keep provider permissions and domain-specific approval gates.

source_types.name: GitHub code / JSON / website
source_types.live: Single canonical repository path and branch (Git commits are immutable identities)
source_types.archive: Annotated commit/branch PRE and validated POST refs plus manifest/history as required
source_types.qualification: Git does not have Google Drive file IDs. Never treat a new Git commit as a new separate live source or require a Drive duplicate for every commit.

audit_fields: original live provider ID and URL
PRE/POST ordinal and archive copy IDs
source revision and hash or commit
restoration path to SAME original ID
safety: Applies to subjects whose owning A7/A9 policy requires enumerated archival. Do not create unbounded duplicate copies for unrelated Git commits, change Google document IDs, destroy revisions, expose private file IDs on public Pages, override original access controls, or claim cross-provider automation is deployed. Where provider-copy semantics differ, record the method and any limitation instead of asserting an exact replica.
